anomalies.observed: The ATO_VALVE net is wired to ESP32-C6 pin IO7/SPI_MOSI on the SoC sheet; pin IO2 is left with no connection at all.
anomalies.expected: The specification's cross-check table states the r2 schematic wires the ATO_VALVE net to ESP32 pin IO2.

evidence.quote: M1A ESP32-C6-DEVKIT right-side pin labelled IO7/SPI_MOSI is wired to the label ATO_VALVE; IO2 (left side) is unconnected

anomalies.impact: Firmware toggling the ATO solenoid on IO2 would never actuate the valve; the valve would only move if the control were moved to IO7, so the automatic top-off function is broken.

anomalies.observed: R5 (10 kΩ) connects the +3V3 rail to the gate (pin 1) of T2 (IRLR2905), the low-side N-MOSFET for the main circulation pump; T1's collector also drives this same gate node.
anomalies.expected: A low-side N-FET gate should be pulled to GND so the pump is off when the pre-driver is inactive. The equivalent ATO-valve driver uses a base pull-down (R12 10 kΩ) for fail-off behaviour instead.

evidence.quote: +3V3 power flag -> R5 10k -> gate (pin 1) of T2 IRLR2905, shared with collector of T1 BT3904

anomalies.impact: T2 is held on by default whenever T1 is off, so the main circulation pump is energised (fail-on) and the control sense is inverted relative to the intended low-side switch.

parsed.summary: The drawing deviates from the intended design: the ATO-valve control is wired to ESP32 IO7 instead of the specified IO2, and the main-pump MOSFET gate carries a +3V3 pull-up (fail-on) rather than a pull-down. Both changes would make the board behave differently from the specified design.
